solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Outlook extremely healthy after botched Polish surgery

indicators.note: after says the ends of healthy come behind the rest
something botched is messed up, so the letters of the word Polish are jumbled

parts.note: OP is short for operation, a piece of surgery

indicators.note: extremely takes only the extreme letters, first and last, of the word healthy

explanation.surface: A bungled cosmetic operation leaves a patient's outlook looking very healthy indeed, or perhaps not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality or the verb, but it is just the letters for 'botched' to rearrange. 'Outlook' means a view of life here, not a prospect.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's philosophy is their general attitude or view of life, their outlook.

clue.text: Queen saves English brand, the height of fashion?

indicators.note: saves means keeps safely within, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: HM stands for Her Majesty, the Queen
a line is a brand or range of goods sold under one name

explanation.surface: The monarch protects a British label that sits at the top of the fashion world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saves' puts E inside HM to make HEM. The question mark flags that 'height' is literal: the definition is about where a skirt ends, not the latest style.
explanation.definitionFit: A hemline sets the length of a skirt or dress, a height that rises and falls with fashion.

clue.text: Where people go at the end of June to unwind

parts.note: loos are toilets, where people go when they need to go

indicators.note: at the end of takes the closing letter of the word June

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers head somewhere at the end of June to relax.
explanation.walkthrough: LOO is everyday British slang for a toilet; the surface makes 'go' sound like travel.
explanation.definitionFit: To loose something is to untie or release it, so it means to undo or unwind.

clue.text: Turning point in star's career is close perhaps? About time

indicators.note: About means around, so one piece goes around the other
perhaps signals that the letters of is close may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A celebrity's career reaches a crossroads; is the end near? Time will tell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges IS CLOSE into SOLSICE, and 'About' wraps that around T. The star is the sun, whose career is its yearly path across the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: At each solstice the sun's apparent north-south movement stops and reverses, a turning point in its course.

clue.text: Left chap due to war reforms in Oxbridge, say

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
a man is a chap or fellow

indicators.note: reforms means forms again, so the letters of due to war are reshaped

explanation.surface: A man abandons the university because of the war that reshapes Oxford and Cambridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reforms' rearranges DUE TO WAR into TEAUWORD. 'Oxbridge' looks like the place, but here it is an example of a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxbridge blends Oxford and Cambridge into one word, the classic example of a blended word.

clue.text: Yankee working with German article over there

parts.note: Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet
on means working, as a machine that is switched on
der is the masculine definite article in German

explanation.surface: An American working alongside a German item, somewhere in the distance.
explanation.definitionFit: Yonder is an old-fashioned word for that place in the distance, at some way off.

clue.text: Where to tie up victim deprived of his rights

indicators.note: deprived of means having something taken away, so letters are removed

parts.note: a quarry is a hunted victim or prey
each right is abbreviated R, so his two rights are two Rs

explanation.surface: A hostage who has lost his civil rights is told where he will be tied up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deprived of' removes both Rs from QUARRY. 'Tie up' sounds like binding a captive but means mooring a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Boats and ships are moored at a wharf, the landing place where they tie up.

clue.text: Strictly feature Fleet Street record?

parts.note: fleet means quick, as in fleet of foot
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A record about Fleet Street, London's old newspaper district, shown on a strict programme.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly is Strictly Come Dancing, the BBC ballroom dancing show. Fleet Street, home of the British press, reads as one name but splits in two.
explanation.definitionFit: This brisk ballroom dance is one of the routines couples perform on the dancing show.

clue.text: A classical way to start to redesign flier

parts.note: via is Latin, the classical language, for way or road

indicators.note: start to takes the opening letter of the word redesign

explanation.surface: Instructions on a Latin-inspired way to begin redesigning something that flies.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot is a flier, someone who flies aircraft.

clue.text: Rounds of decorticated pork

indicators.note: decorticated means stripped of its outer layer, so the outside letters are removed

parts.note: gammon is cured pork from the hind leg of a pig

explanation.surface: Rounds, or slices, of skinned pork meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decorticated' peels G and N off the outside of GAMMON. 'Rounds' looks like slices of meat but means bullets.
explanation.definitionFit: Rounds of a gun are cartridges or bullets, its ammunition.

clue.text: Any girls working with IT voice complaint

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Girls working in information technology suffer a problem with their voices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges the letters of ANY GIRLS together with IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflammation of the voice box causes hoarseness or loss of speech, a complaint affecting the voice.

clue.text: Dry boring piece split in two

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a bit is a piece
sec is the French wine term for dry

explanation.surface: A dull, dry section of text gets divided down the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' puts SEC into BIT. 'Boring' looks like dull, but it means drilling into.
explanation.definitionFit: To bisect something is to cut it into two equal halves.

clue.text: Just pets, I hear, desert families

indicators.note: I hear says the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: just means mere, and cats are pets, so the phrase gives mere cats

explanation.surface: Someone overhears that families in the desert keep only pets.
explanation.definitionFit: These small mongooses live in social groups in the Kalahari desert.

clue.text: It implies Tom isn't able to fill this with fuel

definitions.text: It implies Tom isn't able to fill this with fuel

parts.words: It implies Tom isn't able to fill this with fuel
parts.note: in the cartoon pair, if the cat Tom cannot, his mouse rival can; the name plus can makes a fuel container

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a man called Tom who cannot fill up a fuel container.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom and Jerry are the cartoon cat and mouse: the name implies that where Tom fails, Jerry can.
explanation.definitionFit: A jerrycan is a flat-sided container for carrying petrol or other fuel.

clue.text: Doctor tuned Sierra GT before start of race

indicators.note: before puts the rearranged letters ahead of the next piece
tuned means adjusted like an engine, so the letters are rearranged
start of takes the first letter of the word race

explanation.surface: A mechanic tunes a Ford Sierra GT before the race begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the anagram signal, but 'tuned' rearranges SIERRA GT into REGISTRA. The Sierra GT was a sporty Ford car.
explanation.definitionFit: In British hospitals a registrar is a grade of doctor training to become a consultant.

clue.text: Exhaust? It's part of vehicle in LA

definitions.meaning: to exhaust is to wear out or weary
the American spelling of the rubber ring on a car wheel, as written in Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A question about whether an exhaust is a component of a car in Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exhaust' looks like the car part but is the verb meaning wear out.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means wear out; the US spelling names the rubber ring fitted round a wheel.

clue.text: Smallholder snares superior bear

indicators.note: snares means traps or catches, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: split as small holder: S for small, then holder
U is the abbreviation for upper class or superior

explanation.surface: A small farmer traps a fine bear.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Smallholder' as S (small) plus HOLDER; 'snares' puts U inside. 'Bear' looks like the animal but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoulder a burden is to bear or carry it.

clue.text: Horse will charge regularly after son

indicators.note: after puts the picked letters behind the abbreviation
regularly takes every other letter of the word charge

explanation.surface: A horse will charge at intervals after the son mounts it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes CAG from alternate letters of charge. 'Horse' is slang for heroin, and so is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang names for heroin, the drug.

clue.text: Yell: "Low score by team at Old Trafford"?

parts.note: C is a low mark or grade in an exam
a cricket team dismissed is all out, as the home side might be at the cricket ground

explanation.surface: A headline crying out about a cricket side's poor total in Manchester.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Trafford is the Manchester ground of Lancashire County Cricket Club; a side whose batters are all dismissed is all out.
explanation.definitionFit: To call out is to shout or yell to someone.

clue.text: European piece about cool old horse

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece is wrapped around another

parts.note: an opus is a piece of music
hip means cool or fashionable

explanation.surface: A European work about an old horse that is cool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container, but the piece goes in after the first letter of the work, not centrally.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the fossil dawn horse, the earliest known ancestor of the modern horse.

clue.text: React to bug in US, riding with Charlie there

parts.note: up means riding, as a jockey is up on a horse
Chuck is the American pet name for Charles or Charlie

explanation.surface: An American catches a virus while riding with a friend called Charlie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there' refers back to the US, where Charlie is often called Chuck.
explanation.definitionFit: This American slang word means vomit, a common reaction to a stomach bug.

clue.text: Bouquet hotel sent up includes singular herb

indicators.note: includes means takes in, so one piece goes inside
sent up means turned upward, so in a down clue the letters read in reverse

parts.note: a posy is a small bouquet of flowers
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: A hotel sends a flower arrangement upstairs that contains a single herb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' turns POSYH into HYSOP, and 'includes' puts S in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyssop is an aromatic plant of the mint family, used as a herb.

clue.text: Response to outburst by OU accepting a smaller amount

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: less is a smaller amount

explanation.surface: The Open University replies to an angry outburst by accepting a reduced sum.
explanation.walkthrough: The OU is Britain's Open University. The outburst is not anger but a sneeze.
explanation.definitionFit: The polite phrase is what people say after someone sneezes, an outburst of the nose.

clue.text: Some run escort agency spanning globe

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people run an escort agency that operates worldwide.
explanation.definitionFit: The United Nations educational, scientific and cultural organisation is an international body working across the world.

clue.text: Half-heartedly shake up joint

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the letters read from bottom to top, in reverse
half-heartedly removes half of the doubled letter at the heart of the word

parts.note: to wobble is to shake

explanation.surface: Someone gives a joint a half-hearted shake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-heartedly' drops one of the two middle Bs of WOBBLE to give WOBLE; 'up' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: The elbow is the joint between upper arm and forearm.

clue.text: Agree to exchange letters

definitions.meaning: to match or be consistent with something
to write to one another by post

explanation.surface: Two parties consent to swap letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to match up and to keep up a written exchange with someone.

clue.text: Fight, still holding ring

indicators.note: holding means containing, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: but means still, as in yet or nevertheless
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A boxing match continues, still taking place in the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' looks like the boxing ring but supplies its shape, O.
explanation.definitionFit: A bout is a boxing or wrestling contest, a fight.

clue.text: Prison disturbances backfire nonetheless

indicators.note: read as none-less: without none, nothing, the round letter that looks like zero
backfire suggests going backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: riots are public disturbances

explanation.surface: Prison riots backfire all the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backfire' turns RIOTS into STOIR, and 'nonetheless' removes O, nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir is British slang for prison, as in doing time in stir.

clue.text: Group of beatniks were dapper around pianist

indicators.note: around means turned about, so the extracted letters are read backwards
Group of says a run of letters is taken from inside the words beatniks were dapper

explanation.surface: A gang of beatniks were smartly dressed, surrounding a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters IKSWEREDAP sit across beatniks were dapper; 'around' turns them back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignacy Jan Paderewski was a celebrated Polish concert pianist and statesman.
